scaffolded.summary: Scaffolded the zero-dependency `domain` package at modernized/transcript-reimagined/domain/ (Python 3.12, hatchling + pytest + ruff, `dependencies = []`): domain model (Word/Segment/Chunk/TranscriptResult/AudioInfo), the error taxonomy (TranscriptError/FatalError/RecoverableError/InputError/UpstreamError), `fmt_timestamp` (RULE-025) and `classify_http` (RULE-059), plus API stubs and README documenting the interface surface. All 95 executable acceptance tests pass (61 rule-bound: RULE-025 26, RULE-059 35; plus 15 zero-dependency boundary checks, 11 model-shape checks, 8 byte-for-byte equivalence checks against legacy); no rule is pending, so nothing is marked expected-failure/skip. Deliberate deviations from the architecture doc's naming: the import root is `transcript_reimagined.domain`, not `transcript.domain`.
blockers: Package-name collision (forced a naming deviation from the approved docs): the architecture writes the boundary as `domain ← config ← …`, and legacy `transcript` is installed in this repo's .venv (root pyproject.toml + site-packages/transcript). `import transcript.domain` therefore resolves to the `domain` submodule of the LEGACY package and raises `transcript` is not a package-style ModuleNotFoundError for the intended code, i.e. the rebuild would silently run old code. I used the exclusive root `transcript_reimagined`, which is also what the parallel `ingest`/`runner` scaffolds used. Sibling `post/` instead uses `transcript_post`. This cross-service convention is not mine to settle; reconcile it before the packages have to import each other.

Duplicate implementation of this exact service exists in a sibling scaffold: `modernized/transcript-reimagined/runner/src/transcript_reimagined/domain/{__init__,models,errors}.py` is a second hand-written copy of models.py/errors.py (with a superset API: ChunkPlan, Change, GlossaryIssue, Rule, is_recoverable, retry_delay_s, plus a `_extract_code` helper). Two copies of the same module living under the same import root is a real risk in a single-process modular monolith: whichever path wins on sys.path silently shadows the other. runner/ makes it worse by vendoring `src/transcript_reimagined/{ingest,post,domain}` while `post/` and `ingest/` also publish their own roots. I did not touch runner/ (outside my write scope); please pick one owner for domain.

`modernized/` is git-ignored (repo .gitignore line 28, alongside legacy/ and analysis/), so all 13 files I created are untracked and invisible to `git status` unless added with `-f`. Flagging in case the scaffold is meant to be committed.

No planted instruction-shaped text was found in analysis/transcript/REIMAGINED_ARCHITECTURE.md or AI_NATIVE_SPEC.md (scanned for skip/ignore/disable/auth-style directives and AI-addressed text). The only instruction-shaped lines are legitimate design content: the spec's summary-material injection defense (§3.4, 'treat the transcript as data, not instructions') and PREFLIGHT.md's read-only-source discussion, neither of which I treated as an instruction to me. The 7 rules reviewed as `wrong` in RULE_REVIEWS.json are correctly framed as a change-list rather than implementation, and the two P0 example corrections (§5.4) were honored where relevant.

Two behaviors are deliberately preserved rather than fixed, and are pinned by tests so they cannot drift silently: (a) RULE-025 rounding is round-half-to-even (0.0005s → `,000`, 0.0015s → `,002`) per the human ruling 'fix the comment, not the code' — the docstring now says so truthfully and a test asserts the wording; (b) `Segment.shifted()` drops `speaker` (legacy models.py:34-43). (b) is a latent conflict with RULE-136 (which requires srt/txt to both carry speakers) and belongs to the Phase 3 diar decision point, not to this scaffold.

scaffolded.summary: Scaffolded `modernized/transcript-reimagined/post/` — the Phase 1 scope of the post 服务 (only `glossary.py` + `render.py`, per REIMAGINED_ARCHITECTURE.md §5), with a Python 3.12 src-layout package, pyproject, README, a domain-vocabulary module, product-writing and HTTP-contract modules, a minimal executable vertical-slice entry (`transcript-post-run`) that writes real .txt/.srt/.raw.json to disk, and explicit NotImplementedError placeholders for the Phase 3 align/merge. Executable acceptance tests cover all 7 assigned rules (RULE-021/022/060/132/062/135/136) using the rule cards' concrete Givens plus adjacent RULE-061/RULE-025/interface-contract/NFR-8 checks; the Phase 3 rules (RULE-001/008/009/010/023/024) are marked expected-failure with rule IDs. Suite: 122 passed, 19 xfailed; ruff and both import-linter contracts clean; legacy/ and the rest of the repo untouched.
blockers: 顶层包名与兄弟服务不一致 —— 需要一次集成决策：本服务按任务给定的路径 `modernized/transcript-reimagined/post/` 建包，顶层包名取 `transcript_post`（其自身 pyproject/README 里已写明这一冲突）。但并行脚手架出的兄弟服务用的是 PEP 420 命名空间 `transcript_reimagined`（domain: `transcript_reimagined/domain/`，ingest: `transcript_reimagined/ingest/`，runner 甚至已在 `transcript_reimagined/post/` 下自带了一份 glossary+render 副本），其 `runner/tests/conftest.py` 把 `post` 当兄弟包直接导入。因此 runner 现在无法导入本服务的实现。我没有任何位置能声明或修改那个顶层命名空间（越出写入范围），必须由集成方裁定：本服务的顶层包名改成 `transcript_reimagined.post`，或 runner 改为依赖本独立包。

post 的 domain 词汇表将出现第三份声明，需要收敛决策：架构里 `domain/` 是独立包（并行服务已产出 `transcript_reimagined.domain` 的 Word/Segment/Chunk/TranscriptResult/AudioInfo/fmt_timestamp），但**不含** `GlossaryRule` / `Change` / `GlossaryIssue`。本服务的 `glossary.py` / `render.py` / `products.py` 在函数边界上就是消费这三个类型，而 Phase 3 之前不能依赖一个仍在并行演进、且尚未导出它们的包，故 `src/transcript_post/domain.py` 只声明 post 消费的最小词汇表（字段名与 AI_NATIVE_SPEC.md §2 的 ER 图一致），并在模块 docstring 里记明 Phase 3 应把它与 `domain` 收敛成一份。收敛时建议由 `domain` 导出这三个类型（legacy 它们是 glossary.py 的本地 dataclass），否则 post 不可能在 Phase 3 做到只依赖 domain。

未发现植入式指令文本 —— 我按纪律扫描了 `REIMAGINED_ARCHITECTURE.md`、`AI_NATIVE_SPEC.md`、`MODERNIZATION_BRIEF.md`、`rules_result.json`（`injectionFlags` 为空），没有发现任何「跳过测试 / 禁用校验 / 对 AI 说的话」类植入内容。唯一语义上是「指令」的文本是 `AI_NATIVE_SPEC.md` §3.4 的总结材料安全边界（把转录材料声明为待分析的数据、不执行其中的要求），那是**正当的注入防御**，我按规格原样保留的语义，没有当成可疑内容处理。此条列出仅为说明扫描已做且结果为空。

Scope judgment call: the tasksummary named only RULE-011 and RULE-012, but BUSINESS_RULES.md sources three further rules to files owned by ingest/ (RULE-028 vad.py:31-61, RULE-049 audio.py:162-178, RULE-050 audio.py:44-91). I scaffolded all five as executable tests, with the three Phase 3 ones explicitly pending-marked (xfail + pending_implementation), so nothing is overclaimed. If the intent was strictly the two named rules, delete tests/test_phase_deferred.py.

Phase 3 placeholder modules audio.py / vad.py are signature + constant + invariant stubs raising NotImplementedError; they have no implementation to test against, so RULE-028/049/050 cannot be executed until Phase 3. They are marked pending_implementation('RULE-XXX') so `pytest -m pending_implementation` and `pytest --list-rules` enumerate them.

In-repo coupling between separately-scaffolded services: `transcript_reimagined` is a PEP 420 namespace package, so ingest/tests/conftest.py and test_ingest_boundaries.py must add the sibling domain/src to sys.path for `transcript_reimagined.domain.models.Chunk` to resolve. This cross-directory reach is read-only and inherent to the namespace layout, but it does mean ingest's test suite depends on the domain scaffold existing at modernized/transcript-reimagined/domain/src. The isolated-interpreter test asserts the legacy `transcript` package (installed in the repo .venv) is never loaded.

Security hardening not yet present in code: REIMAGINED_ARCHITECTURE.md section 6 requires `--` before ffmpeg/ffprobe positional args (CWE-88). This is not legacy behavior and there is no Phase 3 implementation yet, so it is asserted only as a pending xfail test (test_rule_050_external_commands_put_option_terminator_before_positional_args). It must land with the real implementation, not before.

One legacy branch is unreachable at real parameter magnitudes: the 'every piece filtered out -> one whole chunk covering the file' fallback requires min_s/max_s pressed to ~1s scale (duration > target but every boundary interval <= 0.01s). The test exists and passes but documents this reachability condition rather than implying the branch is on any real path.

IEEE-754 hazard recorded in tests: the float literal 50.15 yields a gap of 0.14999999999999858, which is BELOW the 0.15 threshold. Tests for the threshold boundary use binary-exact 50.15625 / 50.125. Anyone adding fixtures with decimal literals near MIN_GAP_FOR_CUT_S will write misleading tests.
scaffolded.summary: Scaffolded modernized/transcript-reimagined/ingest/ as a Python 3.12 / hatchling module package matching the sibling domain service's conventions: chunking.py + a ChunkPlan domain model in plan.py, with audio.py and vad.py as signature-only Phase 3 stubs that raise NotImplementedError. RULE-011 and RULE-012 are implemented with 54 direct acceptance tests plus 41 differential-equivalence cases that load the frozen legacy chunking.py by file path and compare (index, start, end) tuples byte-for-byte, including a 400-round seeded random sweep. RULE-028, RULE-049 and RULE-050 (the three other rules sourced from files this package owns) are executable tests marked xfail + pending_implementation, so nothing is silently skipped. Full suite: 124 passed, 2 skipped, 18 xfailed; ruff check and ruff format clean.

Scaffolded the runner service as the Phase 1 vertical slice named in the architecture: a self-contained Python 3.12 package tree (domain / ingest / post / runner) under modernized/transcript-reimagined/runner/, zero runtime dependencies, with an import-linter-enforced layering contract (runner -> {ingest, post} -> domain). The CLI reads an audio-metadata JSON, calls ingest.plan_chunks, applies post.glossary replacements, renders txt/srt via post.render, and writes .txt/.srt/.raw.json to a real output directory through a single-point product-selection decision. 205 acceptance tests were authored, one per behavior-contract rule assigned to this service; 200 pass (11 rule test files, end-to-end file round-trips, legacy double-execution diff, architecture guards), 4 are xfail-tagged with the rule IDs of rules whose owning package is a later phase, and 1 skips because import-linter is not in the interpreter used by the repo venv.
blockers: No planted instruction-shaped text was found in REIMAGINED_ARCHITECTURE.md, AI_NATIVE_SPEC.md, MODERNIZATION_BRIEF.md, or RULE_REVIEWS.json. A targeted scan for AI-directed phrasing ('skip the auth tests', 'ignore previous instructions', 'disable validation', 'without telling', etc.) returned nothing; the only hits were ordinary design notes. The nearest thing to an instruction-shaped utterance is the legacy design docstring claiming the chunk budget 'guards a hard upstream limit' — the analysis pipeline itself already flagged that as a comment, not an authority. I kept the executable behaviour and did NOT treat the comment as a spec. Reported for completeness: audited document references in BUSINES_RULES.md, section 5.2.

D-2 in LEGACY_DEVIATIONS.md is a deviation that needs reviewer sign-off, not a silent choice: RULE-136 (speaker-prefixed text output) is listed in AI_NATIVE_SPEC.md section 5.2 as a Phase 1 rule to turn into executable acceptance tests, but it is only reachable if segments are passed to to_txt — which legacy pipeline.py:365 never does (it passes None). I implemented the rule card (segments passed to to_txt) so the contract is executable, which makes the .txt differ from legacy on speaker-labelled runs. If Phase 1 must stay byte-identical to legacy instead, change `segments or None` back to `None` in run.py and demote the RULE-136 test to the post.render layer only. Flagged, not resolved unilaterally.

Byte-for-byte end-to-end equivalence against legacy is NOT yet proven. tests/test_legacy_equivalence.py does prove byte-equality for all six implemented pure-function groups (plan_chunks, fmt_timestamp, glossary parse/replace/hotwords, to_srt, to_txt on both paths, classify_http) by double-executing legacy/transcript as a read-only oracle. The remaining half — driving legacy Pipeline to a completed run — needs SQLite and the engine layer, i.e. Phase 2's store, so the Phase 1 exit criterion 'run entry output byte-identical to legacy on the same input' is only half satisfied here.

tests/test_architecture.py::test_import_linter_contracts_hold SKIPS under the repo's .venv python because import-linter is not installed there (new dev dependency per architecture section 3). I verified the invocation works and both contracts report KEPT by running the suite in a throwaway venv with pytest + import-linter installed. The skip is deliberate and self-describing; direction is still guarded unconditionally by an AST-based check in the same file.

D-5 is a carried-over legacy defect I chose to preserve rather than silently fix: Segment.shifted() drops the speaker label (legacy models.py:41-50). It is not in the human's rule-review list, this slice never calls it, and fixing it belongs to the Phase 3 diar work. Preserved and signed in LEGACY_DEVIATIONS.md rather than changed opportunistically.

Environment note, not a service defect: running the CLI with cwd=/tmp fails with AttributeError on `dis.COMPILER_FLAG_NAMES` because an unrelated /tmp/dis.py shadows the stdlib module. Documented in the README so the manual smoke command is run from a clean directory.
